|---|---|---|---|

| τὸν δὲ μέγ’ ὀχθήσας προσέφη πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς (16.48) | "Him, greatly vexed, addressed swift-in-feet Achilles:" | "Greatly troubled, Achilles, swift of foot, said to him:" | joins the table's 7.454 row (ὀχθήσας) to the 1.364 row (πόδας ὠκύς), each unchanged |
| νηπίη (ἠΰτε κούρη νηπίη, 16.7–8, of a small girl) | "a little child" | "a little girl" | "foolish" (reserved for νήπιος of an adult's folly, 2.38), "childish" (νηπίαχος), "infant" (a baby, 11.449); the note says the word means a young child here |

| ἑκάεργος (16.94) | "the far-working" | "who works from afar" | the table's ἑκάεργος row (8.323), unchanged |

## Departures from published English

- 16.5–6 (iliad-002 has the line as a whole unit, at 1.201): here lines 5 and 6 are one unit, so the unit is new Greek, and μιν is "him" (Patroclus), not "her" (Thetis). The wording of the line otherwise follows 1.201.
- 16.25–26 (iliad-070 has δουρὶ κλυτός, 11.660): here δουρικλυτός, one word, so the table's "famed-for-the-spear" / "famed for his spear" is used, not "famous with the spear".
- 16.44–45 (iliad-070 has ὤσαισθε, "you could"): here ὤσαιμεν, "we could"; otherwise the published wording.
- 16.38–43 (iliad-070, 11.796–800): the published wording with the persons changed (σέ → ἐμέ, "you" → "me"), as far as the sentence allows.
- 16.43 second half (ὀλίγη δέ τ’ ἀνάπνευσις πολέμοιο) stands as its own unit, identical in Greek, `l` and `i` to iliad-070 at 11.801.
- 16.19 is its own unit, identical to iliad-004 at 1.363.
- No Odyssey lines depart from their English.
